key_insight: X-AgentRed shows that red-teaming personal agents requires exploring how actions chain across multiple services, not just spotting risky single-step behaviors. The paper focuses on compositional failures that emerge when benign requests trigger harmful outcomes through accumulated cross-service effects.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of proactively finding unintended or harmful outcomes in personal AI agents that use tools across evolving multi-service ecosystems. Existing red-teaming approaches often rely on prompting LLMs from static task/environment descriptions, which misses many multi-hop failure paths.
method: Systematically explores diverse cross-service action paths to uncover compositional failures.
Red-teams personal agents in realistic multi-service environments where tool use can interact across apps and web services.
Moves beyond simple prompt-based harmful-path generation by focusing on accumulated effects and service interactions.
impact: This matters because agent safety is no longer just about single actions being safe; it is about the downstream consequences of chained actions across services. For practitioners building tool-using agents, X-AgentRed highlights the need for evaluation methods that catch hidden multi-service failure modes before deployment.

paper_title: X-AgentRed: Red-Teaming Personal Agents in Evolving Multi-Service Ecosystems
paper_authors: Yeonsung Jung, Zhiyuan Wang, Zifan Wang, Vítor Albiero, Benjamin Newman
